programmes.deadline_note: Historically run alongside Trailblazer rounds. Transferred to MBIE with the disestablishment of Callaghan Innovation; current round timing unpublished as at 14 August 2026.
programmes.reopen_note: Listed among the products continuing under MBIE. Confirm with MBIE.

Define the evidence-gathering plan and key uncertainties.
Submit the application.
Assessment and funding agreement.

programmes.amount_note: Co-funding of up to 50% of eligible costs for bold, market-shaping innovation projects, with individual awards historically up to several million dollars over a multi-year term. Complemented by the smaller Ārohia Evidence Grant for validation work.
programmes.deadline_note: Historically run in competitive rounds by Callaghan Innovation. Following disestablishment the grant transferred to MBIE; round timing under MBIE administration was not published as at 14 August 2026.

Prepare the innovation narrative showing ambition, novelty and potential to shift a market.
Submit the application with detailed budget and co-funding evidence.
Panel assessment and interview.
Funding agreement with milestone-based claims.

programmes.name_local: Callaghan Innovation disestablishment and transfer of grants
programmes.funder: Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
programmes.amount_note: Not a funding line in itself. Callaghan Innovation was disestablished by government decision, with its funding and grants services transferring to MBIE and its research capability transferring to newly formed Public Research Organisations. The products continuing under MBIE include the R&D Tax Incentive, the Startup and Founder Support programme, the New to R&D Grant, Ārohia Trailblazer and Evidence Grants, Project Grants, R&D Loans, the Transition Support Payment and Student Grants.
programmes.deadline_note: Callaghan Innovation as an agency no longer accepts applications in its own name. Applications for continuing products are handled by MBIE.
programmes.reopen_note: Callaghan Innovation states of its grant products: 'These products will continue to be funded by MBIE beyond the disestablishment of Callaghan Innovation.' The Biotechnologies Group moved to the BioEconomy Public Research Organisation with funding extended until 30 June 2027; the Measurement Standards Laboratory is expected to transfer to the new earth-sciences PRO formed from the NIWA and GNS Science merger; the Technology Incubator programme, Bioresource Processing Alliance, Food Innovation Network, New Zealand Product Accelerator and HealthTech Activator transfer to relevant PROs. Applicants should apply through MBIE rather than Callaghan Innovation.

procedure_steps.detail: Identify which former Callaghan Innovation product you need.
Go to the MBIE science and innovation funding pages rather than the Callaghan Innovation website.
For the RDTI, apply through myIR and rdti.govt.nz.
For business capability and regional support, contact the Regional Business Partner Network.

documents_required.note: See the individual MBIE product pages

eligibility.other_note: This record documents the transition rather than a single funding line. Eligibility follows the individual successor products administered by MBIE.

programmes.source_snippet: These products will continue to be funded by MBIE beyond the disestablishment of Callaghan Innovation

programmes.funder: Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
programmes.amount_note: Co-funding at 40% of eligible R&D expenditure, historically capped at NZ$400,000 over up to two or three years, for businesses starting a formal R&D programme for the first time. Previously delivered by Callaghan Innovation.
programmes.deadline_note: Historically a rolling application through Callaghan Innovation. Following disestablishment, the product transferred to MBIE; the current application route and whether new applications are being accepted should be confirmed directly with MBIE.
programmes.reopen_note: Callaghan Innovation's disestablishment notice lists the New to R&D Grant among products that 'will continue to be funded by MBIE beyond the disestablishment of Callaghan Innovation'. The delivery mechanism and portal were in transition as at August 2026, so confirm current status with MBIE before planning around this grant.

procedure_steps.detail: Contact MBIE or the Regional Business Partner Network to confirm the current application route.
Prepare an R&D plan showing the intent to build an ongoing R&D capability.
Submit the application with budget and evidence of co-funding capacity.
Assessment and, if approved, a funding agreement with claims made in arrears.

documents_required.doc: Evidence of New Zealand business operations

eligibility.other_note: New Zealand businesses beginning a structured R&D programme, historically with limited prior R&D expenditure. Confirm current criteria with MBIE.

programmes.source_snippet: These products will continue to be funded by MBIE beyond the disestablishment of Callaghan Innovation

programmes.name_local: Aspire NZ Seed Fund (Pūtea Kākano Aspire)
programmes.amount_note: Co-investment into early-stage New Zealand companies alongside private investors, historically on a matched basis, with NZGCP investment typically in the NZ$250,000 to NZ$1 million range per company. Investment is made on the same terms as the private lead investor.
programmes.deadline_note: No public application round. Companies approach NZGCP or, more commonly, an Aspire investment partner leads the round and NZGCP co-invests.
programmes.reopen_note: NZGCP's mandate and the future of the Aspire and Elevate funds have been the subject of MBIE policy review on access to growth capital. Confirm the fund's current investment activity with NZGCP directly before relying on it.

procedure_steps.detail: Secure a lead investment commitment from a private angel group or seed investor.
Approach NZGCP (or have the lead investor do so) with the round details.
NZGCP due diligence.
Investment committee approval.
Co-investment on the same terms as the lead.

documents_required.doc: Term sheet from the lead investor

eligibility.other_note: New Zealand-incorporated early-stage companies with high growth potential and a private lead investor. NZGCP does not lead rounds.

programmes.source_snippet: NZ Growth Capital Partners invests alongside private investors into New Zealand's early-stage companies.

programmes.name_en: Aspire NZ Seed Fund (New Zealand Growth Capital Partners)
programmes.funder: New Zealand Growth Capital Partners (NZGCP), a Crown-owned entity
programmes.amount_note: Investment amounts are not published on the NZGCP website; Aspire 'invests directly into early-stage Kiwi technology start-ups at proof of concept, seed, and early expansion investment stages'. NZGCP also runs the Elevate NZ Venture Fund, 'a $300m government-funded fund of funds, that invests into venture capital funds' (Elevate invests in funds, not directly in startups).
programmes.deadline_note: No calls or deadlines. Founders can book 'Aspire Venture Hours' — '25-minute sessions where Kiwi start-up founders can share their ideas, receive feedback, and strengthen their pathway to investment' — allocated 'on a first come, first served basis'.

procedure_steps.detail: Book an Aspire Venture Hours session or contact NZGCP at info@nzgcp.co.nz.
Present the venture; Aspire assesses fit for direct early-stage investment (proof of concept, seed, early expansion).
If selected, negotiate and complete a direct equity investment, typically alongside private co-investors.

documents_required.note: No formal document list is published

eligibility.other_note: New Zealand technology start-ups at proof of concept, seed and early expansion stages. NZGCP publishes no formal eligibility criteria or investment sizes on its site; this is equity investment, not a grant.

programmes.source_snippet: Aspire NZ Seed Fund invests directly into early-stage Kiwi technology start-ups at proof of concept, seed, and early expansion investment stages.

programmes.amount_note: A NZ$300 million fund-of-funds investing into New Zealand venture capital funds rather than directly into startups, to increase the supply of Series A and B capital. Startups access it indirectly by raising from an Elevate-backed VC.
programmes.deadline_note: Fund managers approach NZGCP for cornerstone commitments. Startups do not apply directly.

procedure_steps.detail: For startups: identify and pitch to VC funds that have received Elevate commitments.
For fund managers: approach NZGCP with the fund proposition.
NZGCP due diligence and investment committee.
Cornerstone commitment to the fund.

documents_required.doc: Standard VC diligence materials (for startups pitching Elevate-backed funds)

eligibility.other_note: Startups benefit indirectly. Elevate's direct counterparties are venture capital fund managers investing in New Zealand companies.

programmes.source_snippet: The Elevate NZ Venture Fund invests into venture capital funds to increase capital available to New Zealand companies.

programmes.name_local: New Zealand Trade and Enterprise (NZTE) customer support
programmes.name_en: NZTE Customer Support and International Growth Services
programmes.amount_note: NZTE provides intensive support to a selected group of 'Focus' customers, including international market advisers, in-market introductions, and co-funding towards specific international growth activities. Co-funding is negotiated per customer rather than published as a standard grant amount.
programmes.deadline_note: Not an open grant. NZTE selects customers based on export potential and scale; businesses can register interest through the NZTE website or the Regional Business Partner Network.

procedure_steps.detail: Register interest with NZTE or through a Regional Business Partner Network growth adviser.
Assessment of export readiness and growth potential.
If selected as an NZTE customer, work with a customer manager to agree a growth plan.
Access in-market services and negotiated co-funding for specific activities.

eligibility.other_note: New Zealand businesses with significant international growth potential. NZTE prioritises a limited number of customers rather than serving all applicants.

programmes.source_snippet: NZTE helps New Zealand businesses grow bigger, better and faster in international markets.

programmes.amount_note: '15% tax credit available for eligible R&D', with a 'minimum eligible R&D expenditure of $50,000 a year' and a 'maximum eligible R&D expenditure of $120 million a year'.
programmes.deadline_note: Annual cycle tied to the income year: register, then file either a general approval application or a criteria and methodologies approval application 'by the relevant due date', then file an R&D supplementary return 'by the relevant due date'. Specific due dates depend on your balance date.

procedure_steps.detail: Check your eligibility to register for the R&D tax incentive.
Register for the incentive in myIR.
Submit a general approval application, OR a criteria and methodologies approval application, by the relevant due date.
After approval, file an R&D supplementary return by the relevant due date alongside your income tax return.

documents_required.doc: General approval application (or criteria and methodologies approval application)
Records evidencing eligible R&D activities and expenditure

eligibility.other_note: Activities must 'seek to solve scientific or technological uncertainty(ies)'. Minimum spend of NZ$50,000 a year unless an approved research provider is used (approved research provider rules not verified here).

programmes.source_snippet: 15% tax credit available for eligible R&D ... minimum eligible R&D expenditure of $50,000 a year ... maximum eligible R&D expenditure of $120 million a year.

programmes.funder: Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) delivered through regional economic development agencies
programmes.amount_note: Capability Development Vouchers co-fund up to 50% of the cost of approved management training and coaching, historically capped at NZ$5,000 per business per year. Growth advisers also provide free advisory sessions and referrals to the RDTI and NZTE.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling, subject to the annual regional voucher allocation. Vouchers are typically exhausted before the end of the financial year in high-demand regions.
programmes.reopen_note: Voucher allocations reset with the government financial year (1 July). Businesses that miss out in a given year should re-approach their regional partner after 1 July.

procedure_steps.detail: Contact the Regional Business Partner for your region.
Meet a growth adviser who assesses capability needs and completes an action plan.
Adviser issues a Capability Development Voucher for approved training with a registered provider.
Book and complete the training, paying at least 50% of the cost.
Provider or business claims the voucher value.

documents_required.doc: Capability action plan completed with the growth adviser

eligibility.other_note: New Zealand businesses with fewer than 50 full-time equivalent employees, a New Zealand Business Number, operating for at least 12 months and GST registered, with a commitment to improving management capability.

programmes.source_snippet: The Regional Business Partner Network connects businesses with growth advisers and capability funding.

programmes.funder: Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
programmes.amount_note: Founder education, incubation and ecosystem support (formerly delivered by Callaghan Innovation, including the Founder Incubator and Technology Incubator arrangements). Primarily in-kind support and access to incubators rather than direct cash grants.
programmes.deadline_note: Delivery route in transition following the disestablishment of Callaghan Innovation. The Technology Incubator programme was noted as transferring to a Public Research Organisation while the Startup and Founder Support programme continues under MBIE.
programmes.reopen_note: Callaghan Innovation lists the Startup and Founder Support programme among products continuing under MBIE. The Technology Incubator programme transfers to a Public Research Organisation. Confirm the current entry point with MBIE or a recognised incubator.

procedure_steps.detail: Contact MBIE or a recognised New Zealand incubator to identify the current entry point.
Apply to the incubator or founder programme.
Selection and programme participation.

eligibility.other_note: New Zealand founders and early-stage startups. Delivery arrangements changed with the disestablishment of Callaghan Innovation.

programmes.source_snippet: Startup and Founder Support programme ... will continue to be funded by MBIE beyond the disestablishment of Callaghan Innovation
